questions.question: Why is it important to stay alert to motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in a car's blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is or how fast it is going. Always watch carefully around motorcyclists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. It means you should drive in the right lane to avoid a problem ahead.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should usually:

options.text: Go slowly while you wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic around you.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up and match the freeway traffic speed. This helps you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them recover from its effects?
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person recover from alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, even if there is no traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic should move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic should move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane ends on a road with multiple lanes. Cars in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing where you cannot see the tracks clearly, your speed should not exceed:
questions.explanation: When you cannot see the railroad tracks clearly, the maximum speed is 20 miles per hour.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, use your signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to cars already on the freeway.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the freeway traffic speed.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic speed, then yield to cars already on the freeway. Before entering, check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have room to merge safely.

questions.question: Lanes moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Highway signs that show information about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about possible dangerous conditions ahead. You must follow warning signs. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: You can cross a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: You can legally pass another vehicle on the right when:

options.text: The vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you must drive off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when a vehicle is turning left and there is an available lane. You may also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle while it moves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle while it moves.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats designed for their size. No adult is strong enough to safely hold a child during an accident or sudden stop. Children must always be properly secured in a seat.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night compared to signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and honk your horn.
You are entering a school parking lot.

questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns you that a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in their driveways with engines running.

questions.explanation: Every quick stop uses fuel to accelerate again. When you slow down gradually and avoid sudden braking, you use less gas.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: When two roads of equal importance meet with no traffic control device, you must yield to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen because drivers do not see other vehicles or make unexpected moves. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: At night, to reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their lights, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Signal your intention to change lanes.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to notify other drivers. Check for drivers also entering the same lane. Never use your phone while driving.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Check them by turning your head and glancing over your shoulders.
